purpose: Teach: バンザイ/哀愁/消防署/道楽/人差し指/茄子/茂木/スリッパ

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんがバンザイをして喜ばれたぞ
lines.en: When you were young, your father used to celebrate with such joy — do you remember?
lines.style: Soft, reaching back through time. Gentle questioning lilt, not demanding an answer. Eyes distant. Pause before speaking, as if the memory needs invitation to surface.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: うん、お祖父ちゃん、哀愁を帯びた歌を歌ってらしたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: Oh yes, and didn't your father sing songs with such longing? Such beautiful sadness in them.
lines.style: Warm affirmation with a tender smile in the voice. Speaking from her own memory, not correcting. Slight musicality when naming the songs. Ends with gentle curiosity directed at him.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんが消防署で働かれた時期もあった
lines.en: When you were young, your father worked at the fire station for a time too, didn't he?
lines.style: Quieter now, as if uncovering another layer. Thoughtful pace. The question is gentle — offering a thread for him to follow. Not pushing, inviting.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、釣りを道楽になさってたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: And didn't he take such pleasure in fishing? That was his real passion, wasn't it, dear?
lines.style: Knowing warmth. She's confirming what she already knows — a small nod to shared memory. Voice settles into certainty. The endearment 'dear' is natural, not performed.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんが孫に人差し指で字を教えてらした
lines.en: When you were young, your father would teach the grandchildren their letters on his finger, so patient.
lines.style: Voice softens further, almost whispered reverence. Very slow. The detail — teaching with his finger — lands with quiet weight. Trailing off at the end, as if the image stays with him.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、お庭で茄子を育てられたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: Your father grew eggplants in the garden, didn't he? I can still see him out there.
lines.style: A small, delighted recognition in her voice — the detail pleases her. Warm and specific, as if she's watching him in the garden right now. Unhurried, almost sing-song with affection.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんと茂木さんとよくお会いした
lines.en: When you were young, you spent so much time with your father and Mr. Mogi. You were always together.
lines.style: Quieter, as if naming something precious and fragile. Even pace, grounded. The repetition feels less about information and more about bearing witness. Slight catch on the names, like holding them carefully.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、お客様用のスリッパを揃えていらしたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: And you were so thoughtful about having guest slippers ready. Everything in its place, just so. That was always you.
lines.style: Admiring, gentle, with a knowing satisfaction. She's not asking — she's affirming something she loves about him. Voice closes softly, almost a whisper of fondness at the very end.
